To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a pH sensitive drug delivery vehicle, octylamine graft PASP modified liposomes with high tumor inhibition but minimal cytotoxicity, which can be used for the delivery of anticancer drugs to tumors.

the novel pH-sensitive tumor targeting drug delivery system (OPLPs) can provide a fast and controlled release in subacid (pH 6.0) and physiological (pH 7.4 respectively) environments, and the degree of substitution of the "anchor", which is a remarkable factor that can alter the pH sensitivity of OPLPs.
the novel pH sensitive OPLP is promising for tumor targeting drug delivery system with high tumor inhibition, insignificant cell toxicity and minimal side effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and characterization of OPLPs and the pH-sensitive drug release of the OPLPs.
the design of pH sensitive drug delivery systems for tumor targeting and the development of novel tumor targeting drug delivery systems.
the preparation of pH sensitive tumor-targeting drug carrier and the investigation of its properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pH-sensitive OPLPs can be used as an efficient and safe tumor targeting drug carrier.

a novel pH sensitive OPLP was developed, with the potential for tumor targeting drug delivery, and it could sustain a controlled release in the normal tissue environment, and a fast release in the tumor tissue environment.
OPLPs can effectively target tumor cells and release the drug at the tumor site with minimal side effects to normal cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "anchor" structure can enhance the stability of liposomes and the pH-sensitivity is adjustable by the degree of substitution of the "anchor".

we have developed a novel pH sensitive tumor targeting drug carrier, octylamine-g-C8 modified liposomes (PASP-gC8 liposomes), and have investigated their physicochemical properties, in vitro drug release, tumor inhibition and cytotoxicity.
the "chain-anchor"-type structure of PASP can be used to construct pH sensitive liposomes for tumor targeting drug delivery, which is promising for cancer chemotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH-sensitive liposomes are a promising drug carrier for tumor targeting.
the "anchor" structure of the polymer chain is a promising approach to improve the stability of the pH sensitive drug carrier.
OPLPs can be a promising pH-sensitive drug delivery system to target tumor with a high drug loading efficiency and minimal cytotoxicity.
